sents.d: A defined shoot-day sequence reduces stress and missed shots.
Even experienced photographers benefit from a repeatable shoot-day sequence: arrival and setup time, a shot list review with the client, a defined shooting order, and built-in buffer time for delays.
For events like weddings, having a written timeline shared with the client and any other vendors in advance prevents last-minute confusion about when key moments are happening.
Building in 15-20% buffer time beyond what you think a shoot will take accounts for the near-universal reality that people run late, weather shifts, and locations take longer to reach than expected.

take: Use the same shoot-day plan every time, with buffer built in.
